app.title: BioAgent Sequence Lab
app.summary: A person uploads a multi-sequence DNA FASTA file, or uses the built-in sample, and picks one sequence as the wild-type reference. Every other sequence is globally aligned to that reference, and each differing alignment column is listed as a substitution, insertion or deletion with its codon number. Totals by mutation type sit above the table, and the table downloads as a CSV report. A second tab aligns every pair of sequences, shows the pairwise distance matrix as a shaded table, builds a UPGMA tree from it, and downloads the tree as a PNG.

task.text: Align a set of DNA sequences to a chosen reference to list point mutations by codon, and infer a distance-based phylogenetic tree from all pairwise alignments.

data.text: A small set of homologous DNA sequences from different taxa or variants, read from a FASTA file; derived from them, a table of mutations against a reference, a pairwise distance matrix and a tree.
data.item: a named DNA sequence from one FASTA record

stage.text: analysing homologous sequences once they are collected, before writing up variants and relationships

mechanism.text: A sidebar loads the FASTA file and sets the reference sequence, which drives both tabs: one recomputes reference-versus-query alignments into a mutation table with type totals, the other computes all pairwise distances into a shaded matrix and a dendrogram. Each tab ends in a download button.

field.text: pairwise sequence alignment, variant calling against a reference and distance-based phylogenetics in molecular biology

workflow.name: compare a set of sequences to a reference and cluster them by distance

steps.here: Upload a .fasta or .fa file in the sidebar; it is parsed into named sequences, and the app falls back to a built-in sample if there is no file or it fails to parse. At least two sequences are required.

steps.step: choose the baseline every item is compared against
steps.here: A sidebar dropdown picks the wild-type reference sequence; the fixed alignment scores (match +2, mismatch -1, gap -2) are shown under it.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each query is aligned to the reference with Needleman-Wunsch, and every differing column becomes a row with its alignment position, codon number, position in the triplet, reference and mutated base, and type (substitution, insertion or deletion).

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Metric tiles count the total point mutations, the substitutions and the indels.
The phylogeny tab aligns every pair of sequences and shows the 1 - identity distances as a square matrix shaded blue by value.
Average-linkage (UPGMA) clustering of the distance matrix is drawn as a dendrogram, with the root on the left and an evolutionary-distance axis.
Download the mutation table as a CSV named after the reference, and the tree as a 300 dpi PNG.

distinctive: Every comparison comes from a global dynamic-programming alignment, so differences include gaps classed as insertions or deletions as well as substitutions.
Mutations are placed in the reading frame by codon number and position in the triplet, counted along the reference.
The reference sequence can be switched, and the whole mutation scan is redone against the new baseline.
Distance is defined as 1 minus sequence identity, and the tree is built from it with UPGMA.
